02

Finding and checking stored records

Search every relevant record, clean comparisons consistently and keep authentication feedback secure.

01

Linear search by identifier

Check records one at a time. Return the match immediately, but report failure only after the loop finishes.

def find_by_id(records, target):
    for record in records:
        if record["id"] == target:
            return record
    return None
02

Filter several matches

A filter collects every record meeting a rule rather than stopping at the first result.

matches = []
for record in records:
    if record["category"] == target:
        matches.append(record)
03

Authenticate two fields

Access is granted only when the supplied username and password match the same stored record.

if entered_user == user["username"] and entered_password == user["password"]:
    authenticated = True
04

Update and persist

Changing a dictionary affects program memory. Rewrite the data file when the change must survive the next run.

record["active"] = False
save_records(records, "users.txt")
Classroom authentication is a logic model. Real systems do not store readable passwords in ordinary text files. They use secure password hashing, access controls and protected services.

Explain the difference between validation and verification.

Model response

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    Use this reference when searching, filtering or authenticating file-backed records.
    Key concepts
    • A linear search checks records one at a time.
    • Return a record or index when a match is found, and a clear sentinel such as None when it is not.
    • Filtering can collect every matching record.
    • Authentication checks supplied credentials against stored credentials.
    • Validation checks suitability; verification checks that data matches another source or entry.
    Common errors
    • Returning Not found from inside the loop too early
    • Comparing uncleaned user input
    • Displaying stored passwords during a failed login
    • Editing a record without saving the changed collection
    Misconceptions to avoid
    A failed first comparison means not found
    The search must examine every relevant record before reporting failure.
    Authentication proves data is safe
    The classroom examples practise logic. Real systems must hash passwords and protect stored files.
    EXAMPLE 01 · SEARCH
    Find by identifier
    def find_record(records, target_id):
    for record in records:
        if record["id"] == target_id:
            return record
    return None
    The failure return appears after the loop.
    EXAMPLE 02 · FILTER
    Collect matching records
    matches = []
for record in records:
    if record["active"]:
        matches.append(record)
    A filter may return several records rather than stopping at the first.
    EXAMPLE 03 · LOGIN
    Check two fields
    if username == stored_user and password == stored_password:
    print("Access granted")
    Do not reveal which individual field failed.
